html:
Francisco de Miranda was a Venezuelan soldier and revolutionary, the forerunner of Spanish American independence. He led the first Venezuelan republic in 1811 and 1812.

Born in Caracas, he served in the Spanish army, including in the American War of Independence, then travelled Europe, met Catherine the Great and became a general in the French Revolution. His name is carved on the Arc de Triomphe. From London he plotted to free Spanish America, and in 1806 led a failed landing in Venezuela.

In 1810 Bolívar brought him home, and he became commander of the young republic after the declaration of independence. Beaten by royalists in 1812, he surrendered. Bolívar and others, believing he had betrayed them, handed him to the Spanish. He died in a prison in Cádiz in 1816. He designed the flag that Venezuela, Colombia and Ecuador still use in versions.
sum: Francisco de Miranda was a Venezuelan soldier and revolutionary, the forerunner of Spanish American independence. He led the first Venezuelan republic in 1811 and 1812.
